CT with intravenous and water-soluble oral contrast evaluates leakage and the surrounding compartments. Repeat diagnostic endoscopy is a selected subsequent option when imaging and the clinical assessment leave a specific unresolved question.

questions.stem: Which initial esophageal management plan best fit {patientName}’s CT and clinical findings?

answerChoices.label: Thoracoscopic primary repair with mediastinal drainage
answerChoices.rationale: Primary repair addresses a leak requiring operative closure and source control. The early self-draining pocket and favorable physiology support an initial closely monitored nonoperative plan here.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Primary repair addresses a leak requiring operative closure and source control. The early self-draining pocket and favorable physiology support an initial closely monitored nonoperative plan here.

answerChoices.label: Inpatient surveillance without an initial closure procedure
answerChoices.rationale: Early containment, drainage back into the lumen, preserved physiology and a healthy unobstructed esophagus support expert inpatient surveillance with the already started supportive care.

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic covered-stent placement across the defect
answerChoices.rationale: A covered stent is a credible closure/diversion option for selected leaks. This self-draining contained injury has no ongoing pleural contamination or deteriorating physiology demanding an initial closure procedure.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A covered stent is a credible closure/diversion option for selected leaks. This self-draining contained injury has no ongoing pleural contamination or deteriorating physiology demanding an initial closure procedure.

questions.explanation: The pocket remains contained and drains back into a healthy unobstructed esophagus while physiology is stable after initial resuscitation. Those findings support closely monitored inpatient nonoperative care at an expert unit with the stated supportive treatment and rescue capability. Covered stenting is a selected leak-treatment option. Free pleural leakage or clinical deterioration would change the balance toward prompt procedural source control.

answerChoices.label: Esophagectomy with cervical esophagostomy and feeding access

answerChoices.distractorRationale: The supplied viable focal injury does not require removal of a destroyed or irreparable segment.

questions.stem: Which initial hospital treatment pathway best fit {patientName}’s CT findings?

answerChoices.label: Emergency exploration and removal of nonviable tissue
answerChoices.rationale: Absent full-wall enhancement on an adequate study raises concern for transmural necrosis requiring emergency surgical treatment.

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic grading before deciding whether to operate
answerChoices.rationale: Endoscopy may help equivocal or unavailable CT, but should not delay action on convincing full-thickness necrosis findings.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Endoscopy may help equivocal or unavailable CT, but should not delay action on convincing full-thickness necrosis findings.

answerChoices.label: Monitored nonoperative care with serial clinical assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Normal pressure and no free gas do not establish wall viability.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Normal pressure and no free gas do not establish wall viability.

questions.explanation: An adequate contrast study can reveal wall nonviability before free perforation or shock. Full-thickness nonenhancement is the decisive finding here; it differs from a viable inflamed wall that may receive monitored nonoperative care.

answerChoices.label: Wire-guided balloon dilation with fluoroscopic guidance
answerChoices.rationale: The long, angulated, multiple postcaustic narrowings and inability to traverse them favor fluoroscopic control of wire and balloon positioning.

answerChoices.label: Wire-guided balloon dilation without fluoroscopic guidance
answerChoices.rationale: A guidewire does not remove the additional value of fluoroscopy in this high-risk nontraversable multilevel anatomy.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A guidewire does not remove the additional value of fluoroscopy in this high-risk nontraversable multilevel anatomy.

answerChoices.rationale: Temporary stenting is a selected rescue strategy for refractory benign strictures. This native segment has not yet undergone a course of guided dilation.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Temporary stenting is a selected rescue strategy for refractory benign strictures. This native segment has not yet undergone a course of guided dilation.

questions.explanation: The obstructing lesions remain in native esophagus above a patent reconstruction. Their length, angulation, multiplicity and nontraversability make fluoroscopic guidance important during dilation. Both dilation options use a wire, so the question turns on the additional guidance required by this anatomy. A covered stent is a later option for selected refractory disease.

questions.stem: Which established treatment approach best fits {patientName}’s pouch and procedural constraints?

answerChoices.label: Rigid endoscopic stapled septum division
answerChoices.rationale: Rigid exposure is limited by neck immobility and commonly requires general anesthesia.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Rigid exposure is limited by neck immobility and commonly requires general anesthesia.

answerChoices.label: Flexible endoscopic septum division

Its scarred location favors expert submucosal dissection. Deeper invasion or lymphovascular involvement would instead increase the importance of regional treatment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which next treatment plan best fits {patientName}’s resection and completed staging findings?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The en bloc specimen has negative deep and lateral margins. Carcinoma extends deeply into the submucosa; tumor nests lie in endothelial-lined lymphatic spaces. Completed CT and PET-CT show no enlarged regional nodes or distant lesions. {patientName} remains active without a major cardiopulmonary limitation.

answerChoices.label: Refer for esophagectomy with regional lymphadenectomy
answerChoices.rationale: Deep submucosal and lymphatic invasion make local margins insufficient to settle regional risk. In this fit patient after completed distant staging, oncologic resection referral addresses the supplied high-risk findings.

answerChoices.label: Repeat endoscopic resection of the healed local scar
answerChoices.rationale: Another local resection does not evaluate the regional implication of vessel invasion when margins are clear.

answerChoices.label: Continue surveillance after endoscopic local clearance
answerChoices.rationale: Negative margins and small CT nodes do not cancel vessel invasion.

decisionNodes.explanation: Clear margins describe local removal. Deep submucosal invasion and tumor in lymphatic spaces raise a separate regional-risk concern despite nonenlarged CT nodes. This does not rank surgery against all possible definitive chemoradiation strategies.
